court: In the High Court of Madras
appellants: Bharani Pictures Private Limited, Rep. by its Manager, Ramakrishna Bhatt
case_number: Civil Suit No. 381 of 2019 and O.A. No. 616 of 2019
advocates: For Defendant: Mr. Arun C. Mohan
judgment_text:
Civil Suit filed under Section 55 and 62 of Copy Right Act, 1955 read with Order IV Rule of O.S. Rules and Order VII, Rule 1 of C.P.C, r/w Section 7 of the Commercial Courts, Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division of High Court Act, 2015 (Act No. 4 of 2016) praying to pass a judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiff:(a) for the relief of declaration, declaring that the plaintiff is the absolute copy right owner in the suit films morefully described in the schedule hereunder as Items 1 to 21 having the rights of distribution, exhibition, exploitation rights, inclusive of commercial, non-commercial, non-theatrical medias, world television rights, world video rights, world satelite rights, pay TV, pay per view, cable TV rights, DVD, VCD, LD, Internet and web based technology rights DTU (Direct to User) and DTH (Direct to Home) rights, and all other rights in whatsoever manner including the future scientific advancement and technological rights for the territories of entrie world including India in respect of the suit films; (b) granting permenent injunction restraning the defendnat their agents, servants, each and every person or persons in any manner interfering with infringing the plaintiff's copy right in the suit films morefully described in Items 1 to 21 in the schedule hereunder inclusive of commercial, non-commercial, non-theatrical medias, world television rights, world video rights, world satellite rights, pay TV, pay per view, cable tv rights, DVD, VCD, LD, Internet and web based technology rights DTU (Direct to User) and DTH (Direct to Home) rights, and also other rights in whatsoever manner including the future scientific advancement and technological rights in respect of the suit films; (c) direct the defendant to pay a sum of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rulees Twenty Five Lakhs only) to the plaintiff together with interest at 12% p.a from the date of plaint till the date of realization and costs of this suit.

The Judgment of the Court was delivered by

G. Jayachandran, J.:— The case arising under the Copyright Act hence, taken up by the Commercial Division of this Court.

2. After completion of pleadings, it was referred to the Master for recording evidence. However, the plaintiff has not filed his proof affidavit and subjected himself for examination to give evidence.

3. The proceedings of the Master for the past three hearings is as below:

“01.11.2019: Plaintiff absent. Counsel present. Request time for filing proof affidavit by 12.11.2019. Defendant counsel present.

12.11.2019: Plaintiff absent. Plaintiff Junior counse present. Request time for filing proof affidavit by 25.11.2019. Defendant counsel present.

25.11.2019: Defendant counsel present. Plaintiff counsel present. Request time for filing proof affidavit, but the time frame fixed Hon'ble High Court expired already. Submit case records before Hon'ble High Court for further proceedings.”

4. Since the plaintiff has not present for being examined and prove his case, the Master has sent back the file to the Court for further proceedings.

5. Today, the learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff states that due to illness the plaintiff was not able to appear before the Master and give evidence.

6. The said submission does not carry merit. In the absence of documents regarding the health of the plaintiff, this Court is of the view that having instituted the suit, the plaintiff cannot take his own time to establish his case. Inspite of affording opportunity for him to present before this Court and give evidence, the plaintiff has failed. Hence, this Civil Suit is dismissed for default. In the light of the said facts, no order as to costs. Consequently, connected application is closed.
